notice: Five corrected paragraphs from teachings 224, 225, 229 and 230. The English is an editorial translation of the supplied Hebrew, accompanied by the source notes below. Other paragraphs and the earlier edition are unchanged.
title: Five corrected paragraphs — Sichos HaRan

units.displacedEnglish: Every man has a place where his intellect ends. Beyond this, it is forbidden for him to gaze, for this is “what is above and below.” There he must depend on faith alone.
units.en: And the general rule is: at the point where each person’s intellect ends, he is forbidden to go further. For this is, for him, the aspect of “what is above, what is below.” He must rely on faith alone.
units.he: והכלל: שכל אדם במקום שמסתים שכלו אסור לו להלך יותר. כי זהו אצלו בחינת מה למעלה מה למטה. רק לסמך על אמונה לבד.
units.he_nikud: וְהַכְּלָל: שֶׁכָּל אָדָם בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁמִּסְתַּיֵּם שִׂכְלוֹ אָסוּר לוֹ לְהַלֵּךְ יוֹתֵר. כִּי זֶהוּ אֶצְלוֹ בְּחִינַת מַה לְּמַעְלָה מַה לְּמַטָּה. רַק לִסְמֹךְ עַל אֱמוּנָה לְבַד.

units.displacedEnglish: I was very surprised when the Rebbe told me this. I had thought that there was nothing higher than the World of Emanation and was astonished to discover Kabbalistic teachings speaking of higher levels.
units.en: And he spoke with me about this, and I was very astonished at this—that there is study of Kabbalah also above Emanation—and it seemed to me that there was nothing higher.

units.displacedEnglish: He said, “Even when you sit among others, you can lift your hands along with your heart and cry out to God with a yearning soul” (see “ His Wisdom ” #16) . The Rebbe then lifted his hands with great emotion and with wonderful yearning recited the verse, “Do not forsake me, O Lord my God” (Psalms 38:22) . The Rebbe used this as an example, saying that even when you are among others, you can arouse yourself toward God with great emotion.
units.en: And he said that even while sitting among people, one should lift one's hands and heart to God and cry out to Him with the soul's consuming longing. And he then raised his hands with wondrous arousal and said the verse ‘Do not forsake me, God, my God’ (Psalms 38), in a pleasant voice of supplication and wondrous longing for God, blessed be He. And he took this as an example: this is how it is fitting for a Jewish man, even when he is among people, to arouse himself toward God, blessed be He, every time, with vigorous arousal, as mentioned above.
units.he: ואמר שאפלו כשיושבין בין אנשים ישא ידיו ולבו לה' ויצעק אליו בכלות הנפש, והרים אז ידיו בהתעוררות נפלא ואמר הפסוק "אל תעזבני ה' אלוקי" (תהלים לח) בקול נעים של תחנה וגעגועים נפלאים להשם יתברך ותפס זאת לדגמא. שכך ראוי לאיש ישראלי שאפלו כשהוא בין אנשים יתעורר בכל פעם להשם יתברך בהתעוררות נמרץ כנ"ל.
units.he_nikud: וְאָמַר שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ כְּשֶׁיּוֹשְׁבִין בֵּין אֲנָשִׁים יִשָּׂא יָדָיו וְלִבּוֹ לַה' וְיִצְעַק אֵלָיו בִּכְלוֹת הַנֶּפֶשׁ, וְהֵרִים אָז יָדָיו בְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּת נִפְלָא וְאָמַר הַפָּסוּק "אַל תַּעַזְבֵנִי ה' אֱלוֹקַי" (תהלים לח) בְּקוֹל נָעִים שֶׁל תְּחִנָּה וְגַעְגּוּעִים נִפְלָאִים לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְתָפַס זֹאת לְדֻגְמָא. שֶׁכָּךְ רָאוּי לְאִישׁ יִשְׂרְאֵלִי שֶׁאֲפִלּוּ כְּשֶׁהוּא בֵּין אֲנָשִׁים יִתְעוֹרֵר בְּכָל פַּעַם לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ בְּהִתְעוֹרְרוּת נִמְרָץ כַּנַּ"ל.
